name: Najaf · Kufa
tagline: Imam Ali's shrine and the world's largest cemetery
summary: Najaf holds the shrine of Ali ibn Abi Talib, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad and the first Shia Imam, and is the centre of Shia scholarship. Beside it lies Wadi al-Salam, perhaps the largest cemetery on earth, and nearby Kufa has one of Islam's oldest mosques. Check your government's current travel advice for Iraq before planning.
seasonNote: Busiest around Arbaeen, when pilgrims set out on foot for Karbala (about 80 km over two or three days), and on Eid al-Ghadir. Summer passes 48°C.
arrival: Many governments advise against some or all travel to Iraq; read yours first. Najaf International Airport has flights from Dubai, Istanbul, Tehran and the Gulf, about 30 minutes from the shrine. Many nationalities can get a visa online or on arrival.
gettingAround: The old city around the shrine is walkable. Taxis are cheap for Kufa (about 10 km) and the cemetery's far sections.
cashTip: Cash-based like the rest of Iraq; bring clean US dollar notes to change for dinars.
foodTip: Najaf's old souk is lined with kebab grills, bakeries and sweet shops; try the local dates and the sweet halawa.
buyTip: Najaf is known for prayer beads, agate rings, religious books and fine cloaks (aba) worn by clerics.
baseArea: The hotels in the old city near the Imam Ali Shrine

connections.note: Taxi or shared car; at Arbaeen, millions walk it.

items.name: Imam Ali Shrine
items.summary: The golden-domed shrine over the tomb of Imam Ali, with mirror mosaics and a courtyard full of pilgrims day and night.
items.expect: Security checks and shoe drops at the gates; women wear an abaya or chador. Respectful non-Muslim visitors are usually welcome in the courtyard.
items.tip: The shrine's museum of treasures given over a thousand years is worth seeing if open.

items.name: Wadi al-Salam cemetery
items.summary: A city of tombs and domes stretching for kilometres, where millions of Muslims have been buried to lie near Imam Ali; it includes shrines of the prophets Hud and Salih.
items.expect: Vast and easy to get lost in; go with a guide or driver.
items.tip: Visit the shrine of Hud and Salih inside it, and go in the cool of late afternoon.
